test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Foundational Full Test - 04
subject: general
question: A and B started a small business by investing a total amount of ₹15,000. At the end of the year they made a profit of ₹2,000. B received ₹ 600 as profit share. How much amount (in ₹) did B invest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of B profit to Total profit = 600 : 2000 = 3 : 10

Since the time period for both is same, Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio

B investment share = 3/10 of the total investment

B investment = (3 ÷ 10) × 15,000 = 4,500

**∴ The correct answer is 4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Total investment (A + B) = ₹15,000

Total profit at the end of the year = ₹2,000

B profit share = ₹600

Formula: Profit Ratio = (Investment₁ × Time₁) : (Investment₂ × Time₂)

 
 A Profit: 1400
 
 B Profit: 600
 
• 
 Total Investment = 15,000 (10 units)
 B's Investment Ratio = 3 / 10

⇒ A profit = Total profit − B profit = 2000 − 600 = 1400

⇒ Profit Ratio (A : B) = 1400 : 600 = 7 : 3

⇒ Since time is equal (1 year each), Investment Ratio (A : B) = Profit Ratio = 7 : 3

⇒ Total investment units = 7 + 3 = 10 units

⇒ 10 units = 15,000

⇒ 1 unit = 15,000 ÷ 10 = 1,500

⇒ B investment = 3 units = 3 × 1,500 = 4,500

**∴ The correct answer is 4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Partnership Rule

When the time period of investment is the same for all partners, the profit is distributed directly in the ratio of their capitals: P₁ : P₂ = C₁ : C₂.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest for different time periods, the profit ratio is calculated as the product of capital and time: P₁ : P₂ = C₁T₁ : C₂T₂.

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and may receive a fixed percentage of profit as salary before the remaining profit is divided based on investment ratios.
